title: USPER Statement about UAP Sighting
what_is_it: FBI 302 interview summary documenting a senior US intelligence official's first-hand account of a UAP encounter involving multiple orbs observed during a helicopter search mission at a US military facility.
core_summary: In late 2025, a senior US intelligence official and helicopter crew conducted a daytime and nighttime search of a mountain range near a military facility, prompted by earlier eyewitness reports of orbs/lights. During the nighttime phase, they encountered a 'super-hot' orb detected on FLIR hovering at ground level that split into two objects and traveled approximately 20 miles at speeds the helicopter could not match. Over the following hour, the witnesses observed repeated formations of four to six orbs flaring up and down in horizontal and triangular patterns across multiple locations, as well as a swarm of lights 'too many to count' moving in all directions.
interpretation_warnings: Extreme redaction: all names, dates, locations, coordinates, organizational identifiers, call signs, and facility names are redacted, making independent verification impossible.
Single-source account: this is one witness's statement (WITNESS 1) as recorded in an FBI 302, though the witness references corroborating observations by helicopter pilots and LP/OP personnel.
FBI 302 reports are agent summaries of interviews, not verbatim transcripts — they reflect the agent's characterization of what was said.
The witness acknowledged that some sightings were only called out by pilots using NVG and were not visible to naked eye, introducing observation-method dependency.
The FLIR camera on the helicopter reportedly could not capture many of the sightings due to the orbs being above and outside the camera angle, limiting potential recorded evidence.
A military training exercise with five aircraft was confirmed in the same airspace during the encounter, which could be relevant to some observations.
An unspecified system test was conducted at the facility earlier that day — the nature and potential relevance of this test is entirely redacted.
The document classification is SECRET//NOFORN, indicating the US government considered this information sensitive to national security.
Timestamps and sequencing suggest some events may be out of order, as noted in the source itself ('possible out of order').

public_headline: FBI Document Records Intelligence Official's Account of Multiple Orb Encounters
public_tldr: A SECRET//NOFORN FBI interview summary describes a senior US intelligence official's first-hand account of encountering numerous unidentified orbs during a helicopter search mission at a US military facility in late 2025. The objects displayed behaviors including splitting apart, forming patterns, swarming, and outpacing a pursuing helicopter — but the document is so heavily redacted that names, dates, locations, and facility details are all blacked out.
public_narrative:
This document is an FBI 302 — a standard form agents use to summarize witness interviews — classified SECRET//NOFORN (secret, not releasable to foreign nationals). It records the statement of a senior US intelligence official identified only as "WITNESS 1," describing events at an unnamed US military facility on a redacted date in 2025.

The encounter began around 5:00 PM when WITNESS 1 and a helicopter crew launched a daytime search of a nearby mountain range. The mission was prompted by earlier reports from personnel who had seen orbs or lights and heard unexplained thuds "as if something had fallen and hit the ground." After dark, using Forward Looking Infrared (FLIR) sensors and Night Vision Goggles (NVG), a ground observation team detected what they described as a "super-hot" orb hovering at ground level. The orb then traveled east and south at high speed, split into two objects, and covered roughly 20 miles — fast enough that the helicopter broke off pursuit because it could not keep up. The ground team reported the orb came within ten feet of the helicopter. A co-pilot then observed, through NVG, a third object emerge from the two and fly off in a different direction.

Over the next hour, the witnesses reported repeated sightings: formations of four to six orbs flaring up one at a time in horizontal lines, then extinguishing in reverse order over 10 to 15 seconds. At 10:18 PM, they observed a "swarm of lights too many to count" moving in all directions. At 10:49 PM, three distinct orbs appeared in a triangle formation within a larger swarm. The orbs were described as oval-shaped, orange with a white or yellow center, emitting light in all directions. At 10:57 PM, four orbs appeared directly over military aircraft as they descended to land — the witness stated the orbs appeared to break off from the helicopter and pursue those aircraft. Five military aircraft were confirmed to be conducting a training exercise in the same airspace. The helicopter returned to base around 11:16 PM.

The document does not contain any agency conclusion about what the orbs were. It is a record of one person's account. Nearly every identifying detail — names, specific dates, facility names, coordinates, organizational affiliations, and call signs — has been redacted, making independent verification of the events impossible.
public_caveats: This is a single witness's account as summarized by an FBI agent — FBI 302s are not verbatim transcripts, and no independent corroboration of these specific events is provided in the document.

The redaction is extreme: all names, exact dates, locations, coordinates, facility identifiers, and organizational details are blacked out, so there is no way to independently verify where or exactly when this happened.
Some of the orb sightings were only visible through Night Vision Goggles and could not be seen with the naked eye, meaning the observations depend on the equipment and its interpretation.
The helicopter's FLIR camera reportedly could not capture many of the sightings because the orbs were above the aircraft and outside the camera's field of view, limiting potential recorded evidence.

Five military aircraft were conducting a training exercise in the same airspace during the encounter, and an unspecified system test had been conducted at the facility earlier that day — the relevance of both is unknown due to redaction.
